Non-blocking observation, not filed as a finding (harm-presence test failed -- see re_fire_context item 3 for the full trace): M5's new '## Say what done-done means' section (learn-from-the-test.md:26-34) is designed to be run inside the SAME M4 send-off session so its answer lands in that session's own transcript ('the original context still live', per the maintainer note at line 124). Neither M4's close nor M5's own Prework tells the student to keep that session reachable across the module boundary, and M5's Prework explicitly anticipates the M4 session may have 'ran out of credit' (line 8) -- a state that would prevent the trick from working as designed. However the prompt's own registry entry (curriculum/prompts/ae101-m5-done-done.md) calls this precondition 'soft ... not a graph dependency' and the prompt text itself is self-contained (no file read, generic done-done question) -- so a student who can't reach the original M4 session still gets a coherent, useful answer from any current session; they just lose the self-inspecting-transcript trick silently, with no crash and no dead end. Surfaced here as a rule question for the maintainer rather than a REVISE: if the trick's fidelity matters enough to protect, M4's close or M5's Prework could name 'keep this session reachable' as an explicit ask; if the soft-fail is genuinely fine (as the registry note suggests it's meant to be), no change is owed.
